turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Aoife, come on in, your mam can sit in that chair. What has you in today?

[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Right so, um, it's the bones. I've sickle cell, diagnosed when I was six months, and I'm after two days of this deep ache in both shins and across the lower back. I'd call it a 6 out of 10, not my worst, but it's constant, walking to the bus set it off worse, and a hot water bottle helps a small bit.
[SEG0003] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): And she sleeps badly with it, I'm hearing her up at all hours. She does not take the hydroxyuria tablets on Sundays, I've said it to her.

[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Mam, it's not Sundays, it's Saturdays, I skip the Saturday one because I'm at the football with my brother and I leave the box at home. I swallow the capsule every morning apart from that, five hundred milligrams. And yes the sleep is awful, I was awake from about two until the alarm, just with the shins throbbing.

[SEG0005] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): It's a thousand milligrams, Aoife, don't be giving him the old dose. Dr Brennan put you up to a gram in January, the bigger capsules. And that cut on your thumb off the tin healed in five days, completely grand.

[SEG0006] person_1 (DOCTOR): Let me say that back so I don't lose it. Two days of pain in both shins and the low back, 6 out of 10, worse if you walk, heat helps a little, and the sleep has been poor. Hydroxyurea by mouth every morning, but you miss Saturdays, and I have five hundred milligrams from you against a thousand from your mam, so I won't pick one. Was there a fever in this as well?

[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, um, since yesterday evening I've felt hot and a bit shivery, only a mild one. I took my temperature at home this morning and it read thirty-eight point three. Nothing like last year's admission, I was properly boiling that time, this is small.
[SEG0008] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any shortness of breath, or pain in the chest?
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): No shortness of breath, and no chest pain. It's only the bones. I stood in the kitchen and took a full breath just to be sure, and that was grand.
[SEG0010] person_1 (DOCTOR): What about the waterworks, any burning when you pass urine, or going more often?
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): No burning, and I'm not going any more often. I watch that, because they're always on about fluids in the clinic, so I'd notice. It's been the same as any other week.
[SEG0012] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any cuts or sores that are slow to heal? I ask that with sickle cell.

[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): No, nothing slow to heal. The nick on my thumb off the tin was closed in five days, no oozing and no redness left. I heal the same as anyone, I timed it, five days on the dot.
[SEG0014] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She lives with me in Drumcondra, and she works Saturdays in the cafe, that's the tablet problem. She doesn't smoke, never has, not even a drag.

[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah I live with mam, that's right. The cafe is only Saturdays, and the rest of the week I'm on a masters in art history, which is me talking too much, sorry. The folic acid I never miss, 5 mg by mouth every morning with breakfast, for the sickle cell, and I've been on it since two thousand and nineteen.
[SEG0016] person_1 (DOCTOR): That's all useful, thank you. I'll read out what the nurse recorded, and then I'll have a look at the legs.

[SEG0017] person_1 (DOCTOR): Blood pressure today is one oh nine over seventy-seven. Last time in March your pressure was one forty over eighty-six, so I'm only using today's. Temperature thirty-eight point three, the same figure you got at home, oxygen saturations ninety-eight percent. Pulse, err, one hundred and twelve.
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): A hundred and twelve? Umm, that can't be right, I was sitting quiet and my heart wasn't pounding. Mam was watching the little screen, it wasn't that high, was it?
[SEG0019] person_1 (DOCTOR): You're right, I had the wrong line under my finger. The pulse is ninety-six, and the respiratory rate is eighteen. Sorry, that was my mistake.
[SEG0020] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Mm. I thought it said ninety-something, so ninety-six sounds right.
[SEG0021] person_1 (DOCTOR): Grand. Both shins are tender, there's no swelling, and the chest is clear with good air entry and no crackles.

[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): The tender bit is just above the ankles, I could draw it on a map, two fingers up from the bone on each side. Sorry, that's miles more than you need, I do this in tutorials as well. The hot water bottle is a knitted one, which is irrelevant, I'll stop.

[SEG0023] person_1 (DOCTOR): It's fine, the detail helps. Folic acid 5 mg by mouth every morning for the sickle cell, you're on that, and hydroxyurea by mouth every morning for the sickle cell too, except the Saturday you skip. I will not choose between five hundred and a thousand milligrams, so bring the box on Thursday.

[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): I'll bring the box, it's the white and green capsules, I just hadn't it in the bag today, which is typical. I know skipping Saturday is stupid, the haematology nurse already gave out to me. I haven't taken anything else regular, only the one dose of paracetamol mam is about to mention, she'll say it clearer than me.

[SEG0025] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She took paracetamol at eight this morning, two of the five hundred milligram tablets by mouth, so one gram, for the pain. That's all she's had for it. I watched her take them with the tea.

[SEG0026] person_1 (DOCTOR): One gram this morning, noted, and I am not starting an anti-inflammatory. The plan is paracetamol one gram by mouth four times a day for the bone pain. And push the fluids, about three litres of water across the day, if you can manage that.

[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): Three litres, right, I usually get to about a litre and a half because I forget in the library, so I'll set an alarm on the phone. I don't really drink, maybe a glass at Christmas and that's the lot. Walking from the bus was a mistake, I'll get the bus door to door on Thursday.

[SEG0028] person_1 (DOCTOR): Hardly any alcohol, noted, thank you. I'm thinking out loud, so my working impression is a painful vaso-occlusive crisis, but I can't rule out an infection setting it off. I will not call it a chest crisis with those clear lungs, and I won't settle the question until the bloods are back.
[SEG0029] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'll book the bloods for today before you leave, full blood count, reticulocyte count, CRP, and kidney function. That's arranged with the phlebotomist down the hall.

[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): Do I have to fast, because I had toast and jam? I read a blog that says CRP goes up in a crisis even with no infection, so I don't see how you'll tell, and my veins are desperate, last time it took three goes and a hot pack. Sorry, that's three questions at once.

[SEG0031] person_1 (DOCTOR): No fasting, the toast is grand, and you're right the CRP alone won't split crisis from infection. I want you back here on Thursday, whatever the numbers show. The phlebotomist is well used to difficult veins, so let them at it.
[SEG0032] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Thursday is her cafe shift, but we'll shift it, we'll be here. If the pain gets bad tonight are we waiting until Thursday, or what?

[SEG0033] person_1 (DOCTOR): If the pain gets worse, or the fever climbs, or you cannot keep the fluids down, come straight back, even overnight. Otherwise I'll see you on Thursday, that's already set. Don't sit at home hoping, if those things happen.

[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): Ok. Thursday, and sooner if it worsens, I've got that. I'll bring the hydroxyurea box, I'll aim for the three litres, and I'll try not to give you the entire history of my ankles again.

[SEG0035] person_1 (DOCTOR): You're grand, Aoife, I'd rather too much detail than too little. Take the paracetamol with food if your stomach is sensitive, and keep those shins warm. Off you go for the bloods, and mind the Saturday dose until we see the box.

spec.situation: Young adult with known sickle cell disease and bone pains for two days, fever mild; takes folic acid and hydroxyurea; fluids and painkiller plan; blood tests planned.

traps.happens: A caregiver or relative reports observations ('the cut healed in five days', 'she sleeps badly', 'he does not take the tablets on Sundays'); the patient agrees, disagrees or corrects one point. The nurse also reports a measurement that the patient mentioned before.
traps.label_rule: reported_by follows who said it. A healing cut that healed normally is a negative finding (no slow-healing wounds) or nothing, NOT a symptom. A disputed fact is recorded with certainty disputed or as an uncertainty. A correction replaces the earlier value (Saturday, not Sunday).

traps.happens: The nurse reads vital signs aloud in spoken words ('one oh nine over seventy-seven', 'thirty-eight point three') and also gives a PRIOR value ('last time in March you were sixty-eight', 'your last pressure was one-forty'). Someone may also correct a reading.
traps.label_rule: vital_signs hold only the CURRENT measured values, written normally (109/77, 38.3, 52 kg). The prior value is NOT a vital sign; it is recorded in the weight/BP entry's own notes only if the schema allows, otherwise omitted. Every number must be exactly as said; never invent or round a value that was not said.

features: disputed_numbers: the nurse reads a value and the patient or relative disagrees or remembers another (a dose, a weight, a BP). Keep both and record an uncertainty.

doctor_thinks_aloud: the doctor lists possible causes or says what they will not conclude yet. Only record a clinical assessment if the doctor actually states a leading or differential impression; 'let's see what the tests say' is not an assessment.

omissions.text: Home temperature was 38.3 C measured this morning by the patient.
Pain location detail: shin tenderness/pain was just above the ankles, about two fingers up from the bone on each side.
Chest examination included good air entry and no crackles, not just 'clear breath sounds'.
Doctor stated he would not call this a chest crisis with clear lungs.
Doctor said he was not starting an anti-inflammatory.
Blood tests were arranged for today before the patient leaves, with the phlebotomist down the hall.
Doctor advised to come straight back even overnight if pain worsens, fever rises, or fluids cannot be kept down; not just generic follow-up.
